title: Adaptive Interference Nulling with a Single-Receiver Phased Array
content: This paper presents an adaptive interference-nulling method for a phased antenna array equipped with phase shifters and a single coherent receiver. Conventional adaptive arrays achieve optimal interference suppression by forming pattern nulls toward jammers while maintaining gain toward the desired signal, but they require a dedicated coherent receiver, frequency converter, and analog-to-digital converter (ADC) in every element channel, along with continuous inter-channel phase and gain calibration. For low-cost, low-power platforms such as small unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) performing Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) anti-jamming, such multichannel architectures are often impractical in terms of size, weight, power, and cost. To overcome these limitations, the proposed architecture achieves full adaptive nulling behind a single receiver and scalar power detector by stepping pairs of N array elements through a prescribed sequence of K = 1 + 3N + 9N(N − 1)/2 2-bit (0°/90°/180°/270°) phase states. From the resulting output-power readings alone—processed in closed form—the full spatial covariance matrix is reconstructed free of receiver noise on all off-diagonal entries, while the diagonal entries inherently acquire a stabilizing σᵣ²/N loading term. Feeding this matrix directly into the standard MVDR/Applebaum (Minimum Variance Distortionless Response) weight equation reproduces the optimal multichannel adaptive weights exactly under ideal conditions, as confirmed by examples with one to four interferers in linear and planar arrays. The effects of the power detector and of uncalibrated phase shifters are then analyzed: a digital detector needs only 6 bits per I/Q channel, an analog detector requires the dominant-mode-rejection correction of the estimated matrix, the random reading error is set by the integration time, and 2-bit phase shifters with 5° rms errors keep the output SINR positive for interference up to 30 dB above the desired signal.
